10.1021_acs.analchem.6c02646: Interactions between plastic nanoparticles (PNPs) or nanoplastics and lipid membranes are governed by a coupled interplay of membrane composition and ionic environment, yet how lipid unsaturation and ion specificity regulate PNP diffusion remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effects of acyl-chain saturation and Hofmeister cations on the interactions of carboxylated polystyrene (PS) nanoparticles with phosphatidylcholine membranes composed of dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC), palmitoyloleoylphosphatidylcholine (POPC), and dioleoylphosphatidylcholine (DOPC) lipids. Langmuir isotherms show that lipid packing decreases with increasing unsaturation and that divalent cations, particularly Ca2+, induce pronounced membrane condensation across all lipid types, while monovalent cations produce weaker effects. To relate membrane structure to nanoparticle diffusion, we combine single-particle tracking (SPT) with fluorescence correlation spectroscopy super-resolution optical fluctuation imaging (fcsSOFI) as an analytical method to quantify nanoparticle confinement and diffusion on supported lipid bilayers. Salt addition modulates diffusion and confinement independently, in a manner that depends strongly on lipid identity. On POPC, confinement follows a divalent/monovalent distinction consistent with the Hofmeister series, while diffusion remains unchanged. On DPPC, diffusion is reduced by all salts without systematic confinement changes. On DOPC, both properties are largely insensitive to ion identity. These results show that nanoplastic dynamics at membrane interfaces cannot be predicted from membrane fluidity alone and are governed by the interplay between membrane phase state, mechanical compliance, and ion-specific headgroup interactions.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c08467: Solar-driven photocatalytic water splitting represents a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production. However, the practical application of single-component photocatalysts is severely constrained by rapid bulk charge-carrier recombination. CdZnS (CZS) solid solutions have garnered significant interest as visible-light-active photocatalysts due to their compositionally tunable band structures. However, photocorrosion and sluggish interfacial charge transfer critically hinder their practical application. To address these limitations, we herein report an S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst (Ni-CZS/MW), constructed by integrating Ni-doped CZS (Ni-CZS) with MnWO4 (MW). Ni-doping markedly diminishes the work function of Ni-CZS, creating a substantial work-function difference with MW that induces interfacial charge asymmetry. An internal electric field generated by the intimate contact at the Ni-CZS/MW interface directs the migration of photoexcited electrons from MW to Ni-CZS through an S-scheme charge-transfer pathway, thereby significantly enhancing charge-carrier separation efficiency. Under visible-light irradiation, the optimized Ni-CZS/MW heterostructure produces 882 μmol of hydrogen. Furthermore, this catalyst demonstrates a strong ability to catalytically reform microplastics, the hybrid system simultaneously generates 331 μmol of hydrogen and upcycles PLA into pyruvic acid (PA). Collectively, these findings elucidate the synergistic roles of S-scheme heterojunction engineering and Ni-doping in modulating charge-carrier dynamics, and provide a strategic framework for designing photocatalysts tailored for plastic waste valorization.
